name: SerpApi
tagline: An API that returns structured JSON for Google, Bing, Maps, Shopping and other search engine result pages.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Writing an HTML parser for a search results page is a two-hour job. Keeping it working is the actual product: Google reshuffles markup constantly, blocks datacenter IPs, throws CAPTCHAs, and geo-varies results, so your scraper dies quietly and returns empty arrays instead of errors. SerpApi is a residential proxy pool, a CAPTCHA-solving pipeline, a parser fleet across dozens of engines, and a legal posture, none of which an agent can conjure in a session. You can absolutely build a local search fetcher, and it will work great for about a week at low volume. The consolation build below is a normalized layer over legitimate search APIs, which is the honest version of this rather than a scraper that pretends to be a browser.
coreLoopDIY: A local HTTP service that queries a permitted search API, normalizes results into a stable JSON shape, and caches responses to disk so repeat queries cost nothing.
requirements: An API key for a search provider that actually allows programmatic access (Brave Search API or Bing-style equivalent)
Somewhere to keep the disk cache
whatYouLose: Residential proxy rotation and CAPTCHA solving, which is most of what you are paying for
Parsers for dozens of engines and verticals: Maps, Shopping, News, Images, Scholar, Trends, plus the hundreds of structured fields inside them
Someone else absorbing the legal risk and the maintenance when a SERP layout changes overnight
Reliable geo and device targeting: results from a specific city on a specific locale
Concurrency and success-rate guarantees; your box hitting one endpoint from one IP is not the same product
moatNotes: The technical moat is boring and expensive: IPs, solvers, and a team that fixes broken parsers before you notice.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because scraping search engines is an arms race you did not sign up to fight. Teams pay so that a rank tracker, a lead enrichment job, or an AI agent's retrieval step keeps returning data on a Tuesday morning without anyone waking up to a 429 storm. The per-search price looks silly until you price your own proxy bill, your CAPTCHA credits, and the hours spent re-reading Google's HTML. It is also a liability transfer, which is worth real money to anyone with a legal department.
notes: A parser is a one-shot build; staying unblocked is not. The moat is a residential proxy fleet, a CAPTCHA pipeline, and someone else's name on the scraping lawsuit.
prompt:
Build a local "search results API" service in an empty folder. This is a consolation build for SerpApi: it does NOT scrape Google, it normalizes a permitted search API into a stable JSON shape so calling code does not care which provider is underneath.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Node 20 + TypeScript, Fastify, zod for validation, undici for HTTP.
- No database. Disk cache under ./cache as JSON files keyed by a hash of (provider, query, params).
- Vitest for tests.

Endpoints:
- GET /search?q=...&count=10&country=us&lang=en&freshness=... returns { query, provider, cachedAt, fromCache, results: [{ position, title, url, displayUrl, snippet, siteName }], answer, related }.
- GET /health returns provider name and cache stats.

Rules:
- Provider layer is an interface with one real implementation: Brave Search API, key from BRAVE_API_KEY in .env. Add a second stub implementation that throws "not implemented" so the seam is obvious.
- Cache TTL from CACHE_TTL_HOURS, default 24. Serve stale on provider error and mark stale: true rather than failing.
- Global rate limit: max 1 provider request per second, queued, plus a daily cap from DAILY_QUERY_CAP. Return 429 with a clear message when capped.
- Retry provider calls twice with jittered backoff. Never retry a 4xx other than 429.
- Log one line per request: query, cache hit or miss, provider latency, result count. No telemetry, no analytics, no accounts.
- Ship a CLI: npm run q -- "some query" prints a readable table.

Explicitly out of scope, do not build: HTML scraping, headless browsers, proxy rotation, CAPTCHA handling, Maps or Shopping or Scholar parsers, ad-block detection, auth, multi-tenancy, a web UI.

Deliver: package.json, tsconfig.json, src/, tests for the cache key and the normalizer, .env.example, and a README with a one-paragraph section titled "Why this is not SerpApi" that says plainly that unblocked scraping at scale is infrastructure, not code.
